tldr: A US customer wants support cover from 7am to 8pm US time (roughly 2pm to midnight UK), starting today. The team sees this as impractical and unsustainable.
Harry will message Pete to arrange a quick call and get a go/no-go. If it goes ahead, Harry will give them a list of what would be needed to make it viable.
Dispatch Cloud testing against a live FedEx account may start today. There are customer-vs-product limitations, and the Dispatch Cloud devs are unlikely to turn fixes around quickly.
Darren's customer portal work is progressing: infra is done, auth is gating customers, and the UI is in progress. Dev is expected to be up and running by end of week.
Tuesday's in-office session with Pete is an intro to North Star and Merak, with nothing new. A product/tech sync on ways of working is likely to follow, but isn't yet in the calendar.

actions.text: Message Pete and arrange a call to get a go/no-go on US live-hours support cover.
If support cover goes ahead, give the customer a list of what would be needed to make it viable.
Try to arrange a call with the American warehouse contacts to reset their expectations on the support cover the team can realistically provide.
Catch up with Speaker 2 and others, possibly with a daily, on Dispatch Cloud testing.
Get the customer portal CX work and satellite services over the line, with dev up and running.

questions: Is the team expected to support the US customer in the evenings, and ad hoc or on a planned rota? Speaker 2 asked, and it was left to Pete's go/no-go.
What has the business already promised the customer on hours and start date? Nobody knows.
Is there enough manpower to cover the extended hours sustainably?
When will Dispatch Cloud fixes for the customer's limitations arrive? Turnaround is expected to be slow.
Will there be a group call after Tuesday's Pete session on ways of working and who is responsible for what? Nothing is in the calendar yet.
